questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with a hypopigmented patch on his left forearm with loss of sensation. Slit skin smear shows 2+ bacilli. Which nerve is most commonly enlarged in leprosy affecting the forearm?
questions.exp: The radial cutaneous nerve (superficial branch of radial nerve) is the most commonly enlarged peripheral nerve specifically in leprosy affecting the forearm. The ulnar nerve is the most commonly enlarged nerve overall in leprosy in general.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on erythematous skin without mucosal involvement. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 deposition along the basement membrane zone. Which antigen is targeted by the autoantibodies?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) is characterized by autoantibodies against BP180 (BPAG2/type XVII collagen) and BP230. Linear IgG/C3 at the BMZ on DIF is the hallmark. Tense bullae on erythematous skin without mucosal involvement are typical of BP.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with proximal muscle weakness, heliotrope rash, and Gottron papules. Which antibody is most specific for dermatomyositis with rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease?
questions.exp: Anti-MDA5 (anti-CADM-140) antibodies are associated with clinically amyopathic dermatomyositis (CADM) and rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease (RP-ILD). Anti-Jo-1 is the antisynthetase syndrome antibody, Anti-Mi-2 is seen in classic DM, and Anti-TIF1-gamma is associated with malignancy-related DM.

questions.q: A 20-year-old male presents with annular scaly plaques on the scalp with broken-off hairs. Wood's lamp examination shows bright green fluorescence. Which organism is responsible?
questions.exp: Microsporum canis causes ectothrix tinea capitis with bright green fluorescence under Wood's lamp due to pteridine production. Trichophyton species cause endothrix infection and do NOT fluoresce. Epidermophyton does not infect hair.

questions.q: A 25-year-old HIV-positive patient (CD4 count 50 cells/μL) presents with widespread umbilicated papules on the face and trunk. Which statement about the causative organism is correct?
opts: It requires sexual contact exclusively for transmission
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum is caused by Molluscum contagiosum virus (MCV), a large DNA poxvirus. In HIV patients with low CD4 counts, molluscum can be extensive and disfiguring, particularly on the face.

questions.q: A 5-year-old child presents with honey-crusted lesions around the nose and mouth. Gram stain shows gram-positive cocci. The first-line topical antibiotic for this condition is:
questions.exp: Impetigo is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes. Mupirocin (pseudomonic acid) is the first-line topical antibiotic as per most current guidelines. It inhibits bacterial isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase and has excellent coverage for both organisms.

questions.q: A 22-year-old man presents with a painless indurated ulcer on the glans with rubbery non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. Dark-field microscopy shows spirochetes. VDRL titre is 1:128. What stage of syphilis is this?
questions.exp: Primary syphilis presents with a painless, indurated chancre at the site of inoculation with regional non-tender lymphadenopathy. Dark-field microscopy confirming spirochetes (Treponema pallidum) is diagnostic. Reactive VDRL is expected in primary syphilis.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman has well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scales on elbows and knees. Histopathology shows parakeratosis, Munro microabscesses, and suprapapillary thinning. The primary pathological abnormality in psoriasis is:
questions.exp: Psoriasis is characterized by markedly shortened (faster) epidermal transit time from the normal 28 days down to 3-4 days, leading to rapid keratinocyte proliferation, parakeratosis, and Munro microabscesses. It is a Th1/Th17-mediated disease, not Th2.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man develops widespread blistering, mucosal involvement, and skin detachment of 35% BSA two weeks after starting phenytoin. Nikolsky sign is positive. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN) involves >30% BSA skin detachment. SJS involves <10% BSA; SJS-TEN overlap is 10-30%. Phenytoin is a classic culprit drug. Positive Nikolsky sign confirms full-thickness epidermal detachment. SSSS occurs in children due to exfoliative toxin and cleavage is at the granular layer.

questions.q: A 70-year-old farmer has a pearly, telangiectatic nodule on his nose with a central ulcer. Biopsy shows basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and artifact retraction. The most common site for this tumour is:
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) most commonly occurs on the nose (~30% of cases), followed by the cheek, periorbital area, and forehead. The head and neck region overall accounts for >80% of BCCs. The lower lip is a typical site for squamous cell carcinoma.

questions.q: A 50-year-old man has a pigmented lesion on the plantar surface. Dermoscopy shows parallel ridge pattern. This finding is most characteristic of:
questions.exp: Parallel ridge pattern on dermoscopy of acral skin (palms, soles) is highly specific for acral lentiginous melanoma (sensitivity ~86%, specificity ~99%). Benign acral nevi show parallel furrow pattern. Subungual haematoma shows blood spots. Tinea nigra shows a filamentous or spicular pattern.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman with SLE is started on hydroxychloroquine. The most important monitoring parameter for this drug is:
questions.exp: Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) can cause irreversible retinal toxicity (bull's-eye maculopathy). Annual ophthalmologic examination including visual field testing and spectral-domain OCT is mandatory, especially after 5 years of use or at doses >5 mg/kg/day.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman presents with thickening of finger skin (sclerodactyly), Raynaud's phenomenon, and dysphagia. Anti-centromere antibody is positive. Which systemic complication is she at highest risk for?
questions.exp: Anti-centromere antibody (ACA) is characteristic of limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (CREST syndrome). The major cause of death in lcSSc is pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Hypertensive renal crisis is more associated with diffuse cutaneous SSc (dcSSc) with anti-Scl-70.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man on long-term dapsone for dermatitis herpetiformis develops sudden jaundice, anaemia, and dark urine. Peripheral smear shows bite cells and Heinz bodies. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Dapsone causes dose-dependent haemolysis in all patients but severe haemolysis in G6PD-deficient individuals. G6PD deficiency leads to inability to detoxify reactive oxygen species, causing Heinz body formation and bite cells on peripheral smear. G6PD level should be checked before starting dapsone.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman presents with violaceous flat-topped polygonal papules on the wrists with fine white striations (Wickham's striae) and similar white lacy patches on the buccal mucosa. The pathological hallmark of this condition is:
opts: IgA deposition at the basement membrane
Civatte bodies (colloid bodies) at the dermo-epidermal junction
questions.exp: Lichen planus shows band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at the DEJ, saw-tooth rete ridges, hypergranulosis, and Civatte bodies (apoptotic keratinocytes). The 6 Ps: Purple, Pruritic, Polygonal, Plane (flat-topped), Papules, Plaques. Acantholysis is seen in pemphigus.

questions.q: A 15-year-old girl has symmetric hypopigmented macules on face and trunk since birth. Wood's lamp shows off-white fluorescence. Melanocytes are present on biopsy but melanin production is reduced. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Oculocutaneous albinism (OCA) is characterized by absent or reduced melanin synthesis (tyrosinase deficiency in OCA type 1). Melanocytes are present but functionally impaired. It is congenital and symmetric. Vitiligo shows absent melanocytes. Pityriasis alba is acquired and mild. Pityriasis versicolor shows KOH findings.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with palpable purpura on the lower limbs after an upper respiratory infection. Biopsy shows leukocytoclastic vasculitis with IgA deposits on DIF. Renal function is normal. The first-line treatment is:
questions.exp: IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schönlein Purpura) without renal involvement is self-limiting. Management is supportive with NSAIDs for joint pain and rest. Corticosteroids are reserved for severe abdominal pain or significant renal involvement. Cyclophosphamide/Rituximab are reserved for refractory cases.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman develops painful grouped vesicles on an erythematous dermatomal base on the left chest wall. The antiviral drug of choice and its mechanism is:
opts: Acyclovir – inhibits viral DNA polymerase after phosphorylation by viral thymidine kinase
Famciclovir – directly inhibits viral capsid assembly
questions.exp: Herpes zoster is caused by VZV reactivation. Acyclovir is first phosphorylated by viral thymidine kinase then by cellular kinases to its triphosphate form, which competitively inhibits viral DNA polymerase. Valacyclovir is a prodrug of acyclovir with better oral bioavailability and the same mechanism.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman has recurrent photosensitivity, butterfly facial rash, oral ulcers, and ANA 1:640. Which antibody has the highest specificity for SLE?
questions.exp: Anti-Sm (anti-Smith) antibody has the highest specificity (>99%) for SLE, though sensitivity is only 25-30%. Anti-dsDNA is highly specific and tracks disease activity. Anti-Ro is seen in Sjögren's and neonatal lupus. Anti-histone is classic for drug-induced lupus.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man from South America presents with progressive destruction of the nose and oropharynx over 10 years. Biopsy shows chronic granulomatous inflammation with amastigotes. The causative organism is:
questions.exp: Mucocutaneous leishmaniasis (Espundia) is caused by Leishmania braziliensis, transmitted by sandflies. It causes progressive destructive lesions of the nasal and oral mucosa. Rhinoscleroma (K. rhinoscleromatis) causes nasal granuloma. Rhinosporidiosis causes polypoid nasal masses.

questions.q: A newborn presents with blistering at sites of minor trauma. Biopsy on electron microscopy shows cleavage within the lamina lucida. The inheritance pattern and diagnosis are:
questions.exp: Junctional EB is autosomal recessive with cleavage within the lamina lucida on EM (between hemidesmosomes and anchoring fibrils). Mutations involve LAMA3, LAMB3, LAMC2 (laminin 332), or COL17A1. EB simplex shows intraepidermal cleavage. Dystrophic EB shows cleavage below lamina densa.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman on methotrexate for psoriasis develops nausea, oral ulcers, and macrocytic anaemia. To prevent MTX toxicity without reducing efficacy, which supplement is co-administered?
questions.exp: Folic acid supplementation (1-5 mg/day) reduces methotrexate toxicity (mucositis, GI upset, hepatotoxicity) without significantly reducing its anti-inflammatory efficacy. Folinic acid (leucovorin) is used for MTX rescue in overdose. MTX inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.

questions.q: A 16-year-old boy has hypopigmented patches with fine scaling on his back. KOH mount shows short hyphae and round yeast cells ('spaghetti and meatballs'). The causative organism belongs to which genus?
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor is caused by Malassezia furfur (and other Malassezia spp.), a lipophilic yeast that is part of normal skin flora. KOH mount shows the classic 'spaghetti and meatballs' pattern. Depigmentation results from azelaic acid production inhibiting tyrosinase.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman develops reticulate hyperpigmentation, telangiectasias, and atrophy on sun-exposed areas. Which UV wavelength is primarily responsible for sunburn erythema?
questions.exp: UVB (280-320 nm) is primarily responsible for sunburn (erythema), tanning, vitamin D synthesis, and direct photocarcinogenesis. UVA causes photoageing, photo-oxidation, and phototoxic/photoallergic reactions. UVC is filtered by the ozone layer and does not normally reach Earth's surface.

questions.q: A 28-year-old pregnant woman has intensely pruritic urticarial papules and plaques on the abdomen sparing the periumbilical area. This condition is associated with which laboratory finding?
questions.exp: Pemphigoid gestationis is a bullous autoimmune disorder of pregnancy caused by IgG autoantibodies against BP180 (type XVII collagen). It presents with pruritic urticarial papules sparing the periumbilicus and can progress to blistering. DIF shows linear C3 (and IgG) at the BMZ.

questions.q: A leprosy patient on WHO MDT suddenly develops erythema and swelling of existing lesions with acute nerve pain and fever over 2 weeks. The bacillary index (BI) is 3+. Which reaction is this and what is the treatment?
opts: Type 1 (reversal) reaction; treat with prednisolone 40 mg/day
Downgrading reaction; continue MDT without changes
questions.exp: Type 1 (reversal) reaction occurs in borderline leprosy (BT, BB, BL) due to a CMI upregulation (delayed hypersensitivity). It presents as acute inflammation of existing skin lesions with nerve involvement. Treatment is prednisolone 40 mg/day tapered over 6 months. Continue MDT throughout.

questions.q: A 25-year-old man has multiple hypopigmented anesthetic patches. Slit skin smear BI is 6+. Histopathology shows diffuse infiltration with foamy macrophages (lepra cells) without granuloma formation. Which type of leprosy is this?
questions.exp: Lepromatous leprosy (LL) shows maximum bacillary load (BI 5-6+), diffuse skin infiltration, foamy macrophages (Virchow cells/lepra cells), absent granulomas, and severely deficient cell-mediated immunity. It represents the anergic pole of the Ridley-Jopling spectrum.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman has flaccid bullae that rupture easily, leaving raw erosions on skin and mucous membranes. DIF shows IgG and C3 in a 'chicken-wire' intercellular pattern throughout the epidermis. The target antigen is:
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris (PV) is caused by IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 3 (primarily) and sometimes desmoglein 1. Mucosal involvement occurs when only Dsg3 is targeted. DIF shows intercellular IgG in a chicken-wire/fishnet pattern. BP180 is the target in bullous pemphigoid. Envoplakin is targeted in paraneoplastic pemphigus.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man has a chronic non-healing ulcer with heaped-up everted edges on the lower leg over a 20-year-old burn scar. Biopsy shows well-differentiated SCC. What is this malignant transformation called?
questions.exp: Marjolin's ulcer is a well-differentiated SCC arising in a burn scar (most common), chronic osteomyelitis sinus, or other chronic wounds/scars. It is more aggressive than de novo SCC with higher recurrence rates due to reduced lymphatic drainage in scarred tissue.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman with chronic hand eczema undergoes patch testing. She shows a 3+ reaction to nickel sulphate at 48 and 96 hours. This confirms which type of hypersensitivity reaction?
questions.exp: Patch testing detects Type IV (delayed-type) hypersensitivity, mediated by antigen-specific T lymphocytes (CD4+ Th1 cells and CD8+ T cells). Reactions peak at 48-96 hours. Nickel is the most common contact allergen worldwide. Type I reactions are detected by skin prick testing.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man with mycosis fungoides (stage IIB with tumour lesions) fails topical therapy. His skin biopsy shows CD4+ CD7- CD26- T-cell infiltrate with Pautrier microabscesses. The characteristic chromosomal abnormality pattern in this malignancy involves:
opts: Complex clonal T-cell receptor gene rearrangements
questions.exp: Mycosis fungoides (MF) is the most common primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. It is characterized by clonal T-cell receptor (TCR) gene rearrangements detected by PCR or Southern blot. These clonal TCR rearrangements are diagnostically useful. BCL2 t(14;18) is seen in follicular B-cell lymphoma. MYC t(8;14) is in Burkitt's lymphoma.
